key_concepts: Food provides energy and materials for growth and repair.
The digestive system changes food into forms cells can use.
Digestion breaks down organic compounds mechanically and chemically.
Ingestion is taking in food through the mouth.
Teeth, tongue, and saliva begin mechanical and chemical digestion in the mouth.
Salivary amylase breaks down starch into smaller carbohydrates.
Peristalsis moves food through the esophagus to the stomach.
The stomach stores food and gastric juices turn bolus into chyme.
Pepsin and hydrochloric acid begin chemical breakdown of proteins in the stomach.
The liver produces bile that breaks up large fat droplets, and the gall bladder stores bil
The large intestine reabsorbs water from chyme, and intestinal villi increase surface area
The digestive process sequence is ingestion, digestion, absorption, assimilation, and eges
